title: American Elm: Great American Elms You Can Visit
meta_description: The street tree Dutch elm disease nearly erased. Oklahoma City's Survivor Tree lost most of its branches in the 1995 bombing and bloomed again.
intro: American elm once shaded street after street in the cities of North America, until Dutch elm disease arrived and killed the great majority of them. That is why every old survivor now reads as an event. Montreal once had about 22,000, and the Last Elm of Mont-Royal is one of the few still standing. Central Park's western edge carried about 500; a 1985 survey counted 23, and the Great Elm of Central Park West is on that shortlist. In Washington the Smithsonian lists its Witness Elm as accession number 1 of its living collection, five and a half metres round and somewhere between 175 and 210 years old, depending on whose account you take. In Oklahoma City the Survivor Tree lost most of its branches to the 1995 bombing, came into bloom again about a year later, and was kept at the centre of the memorial.
